item.title: Oxford Swim and Dive Team Registration
item.description:
The Oxford Swim and Dive Team is a community-oriented summer competitive team for ages 4-18 of all abilities. Practices begin May 26, 2026 at the Oxford Aquatic Center. Costs are $150 (swim), $120 (dive), or $200 (both), with family discounts available. A trial period runs May 26-29 for $30, ending with a mock meet. Register at swimosdt.com or contact oxfordswimdive@gmail.com. Coach Steve also offers a Makos Stroke Clinic for ages 5-13 at Miami's Rec Center (April 20 - May 22, 2026, Mon/Wed/Fri 5:30-6:30 PM, $180).

item.title: Marshall Mile & Family Picnic Event
item.description:
The Marshall Mile and Family Picnic takes place Friday, May 8th with different times for each grade. Students should come without backpacks. The mile run will be in the parking lot, followed by a family picnic on the playground by the swing set. Families can bring picnic lunches or students can purchase lunch in the cafeteria. Sign-out will be at the door nearest the swing set with a green slip system. Schedule: Grades 1-2 run at 11:15-11:25 with picnic 11:45-12:35, Grades K-3 run at 12:10-12:20 with picnic 12:40-1:30, Grades 4-5 run at 1:05-1:20 with picnic 1:40-2:30.

item.title: Tips for Improving Student Reading Comprehension
item.description:
Parents can help assess reading comprehension by asking questions about story elements like characters, setting, and plot. Suggested activities: have students retell the story or draw pictures about what they read. The Reading Corner program uses the UFLI curriculum and offers a parent resource guide. Contact your student's Reading Corner teacher for additional support.

item.title: Welcome Back and State Testing Underway
item.description:
Welcome back from Spring Break! Students returned with great energy and focus after the break. State testing has begun and students are showing excellent effort and perseverance. Parents can support their children by ensuring they get adequate sleep, eat a healthy breakfast, and arrive on time each day for testing success.

item.title: April 2026 Breakfast and Lunch Menus
item.description:
Marshall Elementary's April 2026 breakfast and lunch menus are now available. Breakfast items include options like French Toast Bites (April 16), Mini Maple Pancakes (April 15), Biscuits & Sausage Gravy (April 17, 29), and various breakfast pizzas and donut holes throughout the month. Lunch offerings feature items such as Popcorn Chicken Dinner Roll (April 9, 30), BBQ Boneless Chicken Wings (April 15), Walking Taco with Doritos (April 14), and Mac & Cheese with Garlic Toast (April 23). All meals include 100% fruit juice, fresh fruit selections, and choice of milk. Note: No school on April 6.

item.title: Right to Read Week BOOKaneer Activities
item.description:
Right to Read Week will be celebrated March 23-27, 2026 with a pirate-themed "BOOKaneers - Finding Treasure in Books" adventure. Each day features optional dress-up themes (students choose one of two options per day) worth 10 doubloons each: Monday - shirts with words OR red/black/white colors; Tuesday - fun hats OR sparkly hair accessories; Wednesday - bright bold colors OR wacky mismatched clothes; Thursday - Peter Pan characters OR Captain Hook/pirates; Friday - gold/silver/shiny colors OR jewel-tone colors. Students can also complete "Reading Isles" activities (Mermaid Lagoon, Shipwreck Island, Plankwalk Bay, Skull Island, and Treasure Island) earning 10 doubloons each. Materials are being sent home today.

item.title: Right to Read Week Pirate Adventure
item.description:
Right to Read Week features "Choose Your Own (Pirate) Adventure" BOOKaneers Dress-Up Days, March 23-27. Students earn 10 doubloons per day for their grade-level team by choosing one of two daily dress-up options: - Monday, March 23: Wear a shirt with words OR BOOKaneer colors (red, black, white) - Tuesday, March 24: Wear a fun hat OR fun/sparkly hair accessories - Wednesday, March 25: Wear bright, bold colors OR wacky, mismatched clothes - Thursday, March 26: Dress as Peter Pan/friends OR Captain Hook/pirate crew - Friday, March 27: Wear gold/silver/shiny colors OR jewel-tone colors (ruby red, emerald green, sapphire blue, amethyst purple)

Students can also complete "Reading Isles" treasure map activities (10 doubloons each) including reading themed books, drawing, acting out scenes, and sharing stories at locations like Mermaid Lagoon, Shipwreck Island, Plankwalk Bay, Skull Island, and Treasure Island.

item.title: Miami University Caregiver Group for ADHD
item.description:
Miami University Psychology Clinic is offering a Caregiver Group focused on Understanding and Managing ADHD in 6-12 year olds. The group meets Wednesdays 5:30-7:00pm in-person starting in March. To participate, caregivers must: have a child aged 6-12 diagnosed with ADHD, complete a 1-hour pre-group intake session, and commit to 8 weeks of attendance. Contact: 513-529-2423 or psychologyclinic@miamioh.edu

item.title: Marshall Free Pantry Now Available
item.description:
The Marshall Free Pantry is located at the front left side of the school near the gym doors and is open to all students. For questions, donations, or suggestions, contact Chrissy, Marshall Social Worker at 513-273-3611 or rolfesc@talawanda.org.
